request.instructions:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.
request.input:
Bill number: HB1234

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 313
 By Yarbro

 HOUSE BILL 1234

 By McKenzie

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 Chapter 6, relative to K-12 education.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3802, is amended by deleting

the section and substituting instead the following:

 As used in this part, unless the context otherwise requires:

 (1) "Classroom library" means materials donated to, purchased by, or

 acquired by an individual teacher, which are made available in the teacher's

 classroom to students assigned to the teacher's class or classes;

 (2) "Library collection" means the materials made available to students

 by a school operated by an LEA or by a public charter school, but does not

 include materials made available to students as part of a course curriculum or

 materials made available to students as part of a classroom library; and

 (3) "Materials" means books, periodicals, newspapers, manuscripts,

 films, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes, videotapes, video games,

 applications, and subscription content in any form.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(a), is amended by adding

the language "or classroom library" immediately after the language "a library collection".

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803, is amended by deleting

subsection (b) and by deleting the first sentence of subsection (d) and substituting instead the

following:

 Each local board of education and public charter school governing body shall

 adopt a policy for developing and reviewing school library collections and for

 classroom libraries.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(d), is amended by adding

the following as new subdivisions:

 ( ) A procedure for teachers, or for parents and legal guardians of students with

 access to a classroom library, to review and refer materials in a teacher's classroom

 library for review and evaluation consistent with this section;

 ( ) A procedure to ensure that parents and legal guardians of students with

 access to a classroom library have multiple opportunities throughout the school year to

 view the books in their student's classroom libraries; and

 ( ) A provision prohibiting teachers from knowingly or intentionally circumventing

 the LEA's or public charter school's library collection policy through the teacher's

 classroom library, such as including materials in the teacher's classroom library that

 have been found by the local board of education, the public charter school governing

 body, or the state textbook and instructional materials quality commission pursuant to §

 49-6-2201(m) to be inappropriate for the age and maturity levels of the students who

 may access the materials, or that have been found by the local board or governing body

 to be unsuitable for, or inconsistent with, the educational mission of the school.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(f), is amended by adding

the language "or in a classroom library" after the language "in the school's library collection" and

by adding the language "or classroom library" after the language "from the library collection".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(g), is amended by adding

the language "or a classroom library" after the language "a school's library collection" and by

adding the language "or classroom library" after the language "a library collection".

SECTION 7. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

summary:
The bill would extend Tennessee’s school library provisions to classroom libraries. It defines a classroom library as materials a teacher acquires and makes available to students in that teacher’s classes. It defines a school library collection to exclude classroom libraries and course curriculum materials, and defines “materials” to include books, recordings, games, applications, and subscription content.

Local boards of education and public charter school governing bodies would have to adopt policies for classroom libraries as well as for developing and reviewing school library collections. The policies would need procedures for teachers and eligible students’ parents or legal guardians to refer classroom library materials for review. They would also need to give those parents and guardians multiple opportunities during the school year to view classroom library books. The policies would have to prohibit teachers from knowingly or intentionally using a classroom library to get around the school’s library collection policy, including by offering materials found inappropriate for students’ age and maturity or unsuitable for the school’s educational mission.

The bill would also add references to classroom libraries in Tennessee Code Annotated § 49-6-3803(a), (f), and (g), and delete subsection (b), whose text is not supplied. It would take effect upon becoming law.
